S072.title: Inside the cutaway cliff
S072.bridge: At the quarry, the top drill and the tunnel both pass through floor two. Which column and row identify the cube they share? Check your answer on each slide-out floor.

S087.title: The survey of the L-shaped yard
S087.bridge: One stack in the L-shaped yard can change without either camera noticing. Which neighbours set the back-row and column-A outlines, and what does the scale add?

S088.title: The gap at the parade gate
S088.bridge: Pin the bell float at the gate so a rotation counts only once. Follow the route past the last float. Where is the gap that a straight-line count misses?

revisits.163: Read the L-shaped yard as a stack plan. If you add a cube at the back left, which horizontal floor gains a position? Decide whether either camera will see the change.
revisits.195: When the two drills meet inside the quarry, pause on floor two. Which cube would be removed twice if you subtracted both complete drill lengths?
revisits.286: At the end of the yard survey, raise the back-left stack one cube at a time. Which addition changes a floor count without changing either outline? Which addition finally changes the side view?
revisits.345: At the quarry, count the removed cubes once by tracing the drill paths and again by sliding out the four floors. What would both counts have to agree on?
revisits.171: At the parade gate, compare placing the blue van in the red van’s gap with placing it in a different gap. Which case breaks the rule? Check how turning the road into a loop changes the available gaps.
